title: Virtual Science Museum for Kids
h1: Science museum — a field trip at home
lead: Study before you go. Start at the door and follow the glowing hall — labs first, then space. Free. No account.
printSub: Check each stop. Doodle if you want. Page 2 cuts into hide-and-seek cards.
printHideSub: Cut the cards. Hide them. Write in the box. Ask the question.

habitats.label: Woven Wonders
habitats.challenge: Why do people weave patterns? What can cloth tell us?

video.title: Climbing a giant net at a science museum

habitats.printAnswer: Patterns can mean stories, families, or just play. Cloth shows what people had and what they cared about.

habitats.label: Imaginarium
habitats.challenge: What is imagination for? Could you invent a new animal?

video.title: A glowing sand table at the Exploratorium

habitats.printAnswer: Imagination lets us try ideas before they are real. Yes — mix parts and tell how your animal lives.

habitats.label: Hands-on Lab
habitats.challenge: Why do scientists do tests? What would you try?
habitats.printAnswer: A test is how we check a guess. Pick one question and change just one thing.

habitats.label: Creative Makery
habitats.challenge: Why do makers try, fail, and try again?

video.title: Making in the Exploratorium Tinkering Studio

habitats.printAnswer: Most first tries do not work. Each fail shows what to change next.

habitats.label: Art Lab
habitats.challenge: Why do colors mix the way they do?
habitats.printAnswer: Paints mix by subtracting light; screens mix by adding light. Red and blue do not make the same thing both ways.

habitats.label: Free Explore
habitats.challenge: What makes you curious? What would you look up?
habitats.printAnswer: Curious is your brain asking why. Write the question and hunt for one true clue.

habitats.label: Space Shuttle
habitats.challenge: Why do rockets need such a big boost? Where does the crew sit?
habitats.printAnswer: Leaving Earth takes a huge push against gravity. The crew sits in a small cabin at the top.

habitats.label: Astronaut Life
habitats.challenge: Why is food weird in space? What would you pack?

video.title: Looking back at Earth from the cupola

habitats.printAnswer: There is no down, so crumbs float. Pack food that sticks together and will not make a mess.

habitats.label: Planet Hall
habitats.challenge: Why do planets look different? Which would you visit, and why?
habitats.printAnswer: Each planet is a different mix of rock, gas, heat, and distance from the sun. Pick one and say what you would go see.

habitats.label: Rockets
habitats.challenge: How does a rocket leave Earth? Why so tall?
habitats.printAnswer: Hot gas blasts down so the rocket goes up. It is tall because it stacks fuel under the crew.
